</script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9600"> <h2>#9600. 36 Healthy Fall Dinners With All The Cozy</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Healthy-Fall-Dinners-02-scaled.jpg" alt="36 Healthy Fall Dinners With All The Cozy" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Healthy and nourishing fall dinners that are super cozy, too! Some of my favorite bowls, salads, soups, and more!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on September 18, 2026</p> <p>Fall dinners are here, and honestly, this is the kind of food I wait for all year. Steamy bowls, creamy sauces, roasted veggies, cozy spices, and meals that make the whole house smell amazing. These healthy fall recipes bring all the sweater-weather comfort while still being nourishing enough for an everyday weeknight!</p> <p>To call out a few of my all-time favorites from this list:</p> <p>Nourishing food should still feel generous, cozy, and completely delicious, and these dinners are it!</p> <p>Roasted sweet potatoes topped with creamy chipotle sauce, spicy ground chicken, avocado, cilantro, and pickled onion. My family loves them!</p> <p>I love this Kale Apple Salad! Kale, brussels sprouts, rosemary cashews, apples, fried bread cheese, crispy shallots, and crisp apple maple dressing!</p> <p>Silky carrot soup topped with spiced ground beef and toasty pine nuts! Bright, savory, warming, all the best things!</p> <p>Amazingly creamy, saucy chickpea curry served over rice with a dollop of chili crisp and a side of cucumber salad. Ready in 20 minutes!</p> <p>One of my family’s favorite easy dinners that works SO well for meal prep! Sweet potatoes and ground beef get dolloped with a creamy high protein street corn style dip that is bonkers delicious.</p> <p>Detox Crockpot Lentil Soup – a clean and simple soup made with onions, garlic, carrots, olive oil, squash, and LENTILS! Super healthy and easy to make.</p> <p>The BEST Grain Bowl! Roasted root vegetables, earthy grains, dried fruit, dark leafy greens, buttery goat cheese, and lusciously creamy balsamic dressing.</p> <p>Coconut Curry Salmon! Broiled salmon with a salty-sweet spice rub, creamy coconut curry sauce, and steamy rice to soak it all up.</p> <p>These tempeh bowls are a true fall favorite! Massaged kale, sweet potatoes, roasty marinated maple-mustard tempeh, crunchy apple, and an unexpected pile of briney sauerkraut.</p> <p>Lemongrass, ginger, shallot, and the brightness of lime! These broth bowls have got it all – luscious broth, fluffy rice, protein, and fresh herbs.</p> <p>Saucy shredded chicken, yellow rice, pickled onions, greens, and cilantro pesto on top. It’s a flavor and color delight!</p> <p>We are living our best bowl life this week. Seasoned sweet potato wedges and chicken meatballs or rotisserie chicken all piled onto a plate with a little puddle of punchy green avocado mojo sauce. Yes, wow, repeat.</p> <p>This 7-Layer Beet Salad is a stunner! Studded with cooked beets, supremed oranges, chopped pistachios, creamy truffle ricotta, and a bit of fresh mint. So fresh, so good!</p> <p>These House Favorite Brussels Sprouts are the best side veg and are speckled with bright bursts of cranberries and nutty walnuts. The perfect addition to any meal!</p> <p>These Spicy Peanut Tofu Bowls are a meal prep / weeknight dinner life-saver! Crispy tofu, roasted veggies, fluffy rice, and a spicy sweet peanut sauce all over top.</p> <p>These beauties need to be on your table! Deeply roasted rainbow carrots, swizzles of tangy garlicky yogurt sauce, a golden drizzle of honey, and festive pistachio crunches on top.</p> <p>Healing Chicken and Rice Soup that is limey, salty, and so fresh! Garlic-ginger-infused broth, shredded chicken thighs, tender jasmine rice, fresh herbs, and peanuts. YUM.</p> <p>Brussels & Kale Caesar! Papery-thin shreds of brussels sprouts and chopped lacinato kale, tossed with a creamy, garlicky, avocado-based vegan caesar dressing, topped off with the most addicting cheezy garlic croutons.</p> <p>Autumn Glow Salad with Lemon Dressing – a MUST for healthy, glowy eating! Roasted cauliflower, sweet potato, grains, and apples.</p> <p>Healthy and versatile bowls that come together under a generous drizzle of addictingly creamy vegan chipotle tahini sauce.</p> <p>A savory coconut creamy broth, swirls of chili oil floating on top, beautiful veg and cubes of flavor-soaked tofu, and a pile of steamy rice at your service.</p> <p>A cozy, hearty, humble bowl of this Country Chicken Stew is waiting for you! Chicken, thick-cut bacon, navy beans, veggies, and fresh herbs all simmering in one big pot. It’s a good one, friends!</p> <p>This Hot Honey Salmon is giving off major fancy-to-eat-but-not-fancy-to-make vibes. Spicy-sweet salmon coated in fresh garlic, stone ground mustard, sweet honey, and flecks of red peppers flakes. It’s a magical little number!</p> <p>Harissa Chickpeas with Whipped Feta! Perfectly spicy/saucy/tomato-y chickpeas smothered in creamy, garlicky whipped feta and served with naan, lemons, and cucumbers. Your next weeknight wonder!</p> <p>Easy Veggie Enchiladas! Saucy, cheese, filling, cozy, and packed with any roasted veggies you want. Super versatile and easy to make!</p> <p>Guess what’s for dinner? Creamy, spicy, delicious red curry lentils, made in the Instant Pot.</p> <p>Amazing Mushroom Bowls with Kale Pesto! Smoky, sweet, salt mushrooms (or tempeh!), caramelized pineapple, peppers, and dollop of kale pesto, all served over rice.</p> <p>Sesame Beef and Broccoli! Full of protein, green broccoli goodness, and sticky-sweet garlic and ginger flavor. Perfect at-home takeout!</p> <p>Creamy Thai Sweet Potato Curry – packed with nutrition! Our favorite easy, healthy, winter comfort food recipe.</p> <p>These Roasted Cauliflower Hummus Bowls are LIFE-CHANGING. A bed of garlicky creamy hummus, piled high with spiced roasted cauliflower, and a speckling of fresh lemony tomatoes and herbs.</p> <p>Spicy Shrimp with Cauliflower Mash and Garlic Kale – tender-sweet shrimp and smoky garlic kale over creamy cauliflower mash. The most DELICIOUS fake-fancy weeknight dinner!</p> <p>Roasted Vegetable Bowls! Crispy tender roasted veggies, buttery avocado, all together in a bowl with a drizzle of green tahini sauce.</p> <p>15 Minute Meal Prep Cilantro Lime Chicken and Lentils! The BEST easy protein powerhouse meal prep. Just 15 mins of prep and totally hands-off cooking!</p> <p>Instant Pot Sweet Potato Tortilla Soup! A smoky, limey, tomato-rich broth with onion, garlic, jalapeño, crispy tortilla strips, and tender chunks of sweet potato.</p> <p>These healthy chipotle sweet potato skins are stuffed with a chipotle-sweet potato filling, black beans, corn, and topped with cheese. SO GOOD.</p> <p>Healing Bowls: turmeric sweet potatoes, brown rice, red quinoa, arugula, poached egg, lemon dressing.</p> <p>Fall is for snacking, too! Here are some of my favorite healthy snacks – for myself, or for my kids’ lunchboxes!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I made the roasted squash and lentil bowl from this list and it was exactly the kind of dinner I wanted — filling enough that nobody went hunting for snacks afterwards. More of these please, especially anything with a shortcut using canned beans or pre-cooked grains.</p> <p>Grouping fall dinners by how much time they take, rather than by ingredient, is what makes a list like this usable on a weeknight, and mixing tray bakes with one-pot meals covers the range well. Marking which ones reheat well would help anyone cooking ahead. Turning a single finished-dish photo into a short clip is something AI Fruit does from one prompt.AI Fruit.</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format. Enter your email and we'll send it right over!</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://pinchofyum.com/healthy-fall-dinners" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9599"> <h2>#9599. Rising Fentanyl Use Challenges Current Methadone Induction Protocols</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2023/09/PSYCH_1000x1000.png" alt="Rising Fentanyl Use Challenges Current Methadone Induction Protocols" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>An increasing number of PAs and nurse practitioners (NPs) are working in addiction medicine including opioid treatment programs (OTPs) where they are increasingly able to practice autonomously. A recently released commentary in the Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment highlights the challenges that practitioners at OTPs face in reaching therapeutic doses of methadone for patients who are using fentanyl instead of heroin.1 The commentary authors noted that with “fentanyl’s increased potency when compared to other opioids, many papers have described the need for higher doses of methadone to achieve the therapeutic goal of reducing and suppressing opioid withdrawal and subsequent illicit ongoing fentanyl use.”</p> <p>The commentary authors make several key observations and related recommendations. One key finding is that patients using fentanyl who enter OTPs may view the increased time needed to achieve an effective dose of methadone as evidence that methadone treatment will not work for them, and that this may serve as yet another barrier to treatment.</p> <p>Current guidelines for methadone treatment by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) recommend a maximum initial dose of 30 mg per federal OTP regulations, which were established before synthetic opioids became the leading cause of opioid-involved deaths in the United States. Guidelines state that the dose may be increased by 5 mg to 10 mg every 3 to 5 days. This dosing schedule may be ineffective for patients using fentanyl given their higher tolerance; it may take up to a month or more to reach an effective methadone dose in these patients.</p> <p>The commentary authors offer several points to consider when adapting induction protocols to meet the therapeutic needs of patients using fentanyl and noted that change can be achieved without lengthy regulatory reform. The authors offer evidence from several US studies in which a more rapid methadone induction schedule allowed achievement of therapeutic doses more quickly without an increase in the risk for overdose, which is highest risk during the first few weeks of methadone induction in OTP settings.</p> <p>This evidence indicates that OTP providers are attempting to address these concerns with a variety of induction variations, suggesting that more research focused on patients using fentanyl is needed.</p> <p>This commentary is valuable in attempting to spur further innovative efforts to adapt the methadone OTP model to meet the challenges presented by the greater potency of fentanyl. Engagement early in induction can be challenging for any patient with opioid use disorder seeking treatment. Even before the rise in fentanyl use, many patients with opioid use disorder struggled with the induction period when they were initiated on doses that do little early on to suppress withdrawal symptoms, which are common. This problem is even greater now with the rise in fentanyl use, and this commentary demonstrates the need for OTPs to offer a model for how OTPs and OTP regulators can design more effective induction protocols that are both safe and effective.</p> <p>This article originally appeared on Clinical Advisor</p> <p>Buresh M, Nahvi S, Steiger S, Weinstein ZM. Adapting methadone inductions to the fentanyl era. J Subst Abuse Treat. 2022;141:108832. doi:10.1016/j.jsat.2022.108832</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/addiction/opioid-related-disorder/fentanyl-challenges-current-methadone-induction-protocols/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9598"> <h2>#9598. The Everyday Nutrient Linked To 32% Lower Dementia Risk</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/eggs-3.jpg" alt="The Everyday Nutrient Linked To 32% Lower Dementia Risk" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Your brain uses this nutrient for memory, but its relationship with dementia risk is more complicated than “more is better”.</p> <p>Your brain uses this nutrient for memory, but its relationship with dementia risk is more complicated than “more is better”.</p> <p>Moderate intake of choline, a nutrient found in eggs, fish and legumes, is linked to a lower risk of dementia.</p> <p>Older adults consuming moderately high amounts had a 32 percent lower dementia risk than those consuming the least.</p> <p>However, the highest intake was not associated with a clear benefit, suggesting that more is not necessarily better.</p> <p>The research followed over 5,000 American adults, whose average age was almost 69, for around eight years.</p> <p>Participants were initially free of dementia but around 500 developed the condition during follow-up.</p> <p>After dividing participants into five groups according to choline intake, the researchers found a 32 percent lower dementia risk in the second-highest group than in the lowest, after accounting for other factors.</p> <p>However, there was no statistically clear reduction in the highest-intake group.</p> <p>The result therefore points towards a potentially beneficial range, rather than a steady fall in risk with every increase in consumption.</p> <p>The researchers then combined their results with four previous studies to assess the broader pattern.</p> <p>Together, these followed almost 138,000 people and recorded around 2,500 cases of dementia.</p> <p>In the combined analysis, dementia risk fell as choline intake rose to approximately 465 milligrams per day, with no further reduction beyond that level.</p> <p>Choline helps the brain produce acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in learning and memory.</p> <p>It also supplies building blocks for the membranes surrounding brain cells, helping maintain their structure and communication.</p> <p>These roles could help explain a link between choline and cognitive ageing, although they do not prove that consuming more prevents dementia.</p> <p>The nutrient also participates in processes that regulate homocysteine, a substance linked to problems with blood vessels and cognitive function.</p> <p>Eggs, meat, poultry and nuts were among the main sources of choline in the American participants’ diets.</p> <p>People consuming more choline obtained a greater proportion of it from eggs.</p> <p>Crucially, the analysis assessed choline from food and did not include intake from supplements.</p> <p>The findings therefore cannot establish whether choline supplements would lower dementia risk.</p> <p>The study was published in the Nutrition Journal (Chen et al., 2026).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. No spam, ever.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/10/nutrient-32-lower-dementia.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9597"> <h2>#9597. Vienna Recession? Four galleries in Austrian capital shut shop amid a tougher market</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://cdn.sanity.io/images/cxgd3urn/production/408d3056b2088a6d751eea6efc3cec1bf7d45e91-3600x2400.jpg?rect=0,120,3600,2160&w=1200&h=720&q=85&fit=crop&auto=format" alt="Vienna Recession? Four galleries in Austrian capital shut shop amid a tougher market" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>MYMOVE (pink) by Lena Henke on the roster of Layr Gallery, which is moving to a more flexible gallery model Nils Jorgensen/Alamy Stock Photo</p> <p>Vienna’s contemporary art scene seems to be collapsing. Three of its galleries—Layr, Exile and Zeller van Almsick—are either closing or “evolving”, all citing the unsustainability of running increasingly costly businesses in an unpredictable market. Meanwhile Eva Presenhuber, who opened a space in Vienna in 2022, has confirmed she is also leaving the Austrian capital amid a downturn in sales.</p> <p>Those that have confirmed they are closing for good—Exile after 18 years and Zeller van Almsick after nearly ten—are clear-eyed. “There is no point in sugarcoating the fact that the past two years have been financially extremely challenging,” says Magdalena Zeller, a co-founder of Zeller van Almsick. For Christian Siekmeier, the founder of Exile, “there are simply no new collectors emerging”.</p> <p>Emanuel Layr, who is closing his corner-hugging Layr gallery in favour of a more nomadic, project-based business (including a smaller, by-appointment space in Vienna), says: “The gallery model as we know it is increasingly reaching its limits.” The relentless commitments, to art fairs and the customary six-weekly exhibition, are not paying off. “It’s harder to sell some things, costs are getting higher, then there’s a big art fair coming and taking another €100,000,” he says. “I had to be more realistic, and think, ‘How much profit do I get? How much does the artist get?’.”</p> <p>A historic garage was the venue for the Astoria Artshow, which debuted in September © Carmen Alber/Astoria Artshow</p> <p>Yet Layr and his Viennese counterparts identify a groundswell of enthusiasm from younger generations. September’s new Astoria Artshow, an event held in Europe’s oldest garage (founded in 1918), was a hit, and notably from a young crowd. Its cash tills might not have been ringing, but galleries paid only €500 to participate so had much less to lose. The gallery-led gathering, which returns as a “fair” next year, seemed a breath of fresh air in the slot of previous events, such as Viennacontemporary, which is not showing any sign of returning.</p> <p>Long-time collectors were also fans of Astoria Artshow. “This will be the future,” says Eva Frey, who with her husband Manfred has been buying contemporary art for more than 30 years, and who sits on the board of Mumok, another bright spot in Vienna’s cultural offerings. Frey points out that the gallery closures will come after the city’s unique, month-long Curated By festival, supported by the city and state and which has been a boon to the contemporary art scene since it launched in 2009.</p> <p>Frey says that the issue for Vienna’s cutting-edge galleries is that collectors of her vintage (which she defines as “over 70”) are not enough to keep business going. The problem, she says, is not so much the youngest generations, but that “there are fewer people between 45 and 55, who are established in a profession, and who used to be the main collectors in the market”. Layr finds too that “for middle-income professionals, there is less money around, so they are more careful”.</p> <p>Many of the issues might be Vienna-related. It’s a small market and Zeller identifies “a significant gap between the cultural importance of the city and the depth of its local collector base”. But the middle-income strains seem a microcosm of what is happening in the wider art market, namely plenty of enthusiasm from the younger generations and a relative handful of older buyers keeping the top end just about managing. This requires a holding pattern of flexibility, at best, from the galleries who stick it out. For those that do, and can, hope rests on the juniors, but we just might have to wait a while to know if they can fill the gaps.</p> <p>Third biannual of strongly supported contemporary decorative arts</p> <p>But 85% say market for Modern British and contemporary art will remain as strong or fare better in 2016</p> <p>The divide between primary and secondary markets blur as sales skew in favour of a few recognised, bankable artists</p> <p>New book explores some of the myths of the international trade</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/04/vienna-recession-four-galleries-in-austrian-capital-shut-shop-amid-a-tougher-market" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9596"> <h2>#9596. The Best Food Gifts Under $25 (That Feel Thoughtful and Chic)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://platform.eater.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/The-Best-Gifts-Under-25-Dollars.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,10.732984293194,100,78.534031413613" alt="The Best Food Gifts Under $25 (That Feel Thoughtful and Chic)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Spoil them with a stoneware mugs, princess cake-inspired soap, and a charming Kewpie mayo ornament</p> <p>If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.</p> <p>Eater’s under-$25 holiday gift guide is, unabashedly, one of my favorites to curate during gift guide season — both as a shopping writer and a writer who lives, laughs, loves to shop. I live for the thrill of a thrifty find; that rush of finding the perfect gift that somehow comes in way under budget is a sensation I first experienced while thrifting with my mom as a kid, when I was taught to sniff out authentic English ironstone bowls like an Antiques Roadshow bloodhound. I have been John Wick-training for this moment.</p> <p>The best gifts under $25 for the true food freaks in your life (including yourself) should speak to their specific culinary obsessions, tastebuds, and cult-fave restaurants. Keep an eye out for those limited-edition holiday gifts that are going to sell out soon, and, when you see a potential present, ask yourself: does it inspire whimsy? Why should I settle for a spoon rest that isn’t shaped like ravioli? Move those mugs and snacks from heritage and indie brands to the front of the line, and maybe even click add-to-cart twice so that you, too, can experience the magic of Spaghetti Dust.</p> <p>Whether you’re looking for a White Elephant present or an offering to impress your in-laws, let’s shop for the best food- and drink-related gifts under $25.</p> <p>Diaspora Spice Co. is one of my favorite places to buy spices online, because the selection is always exciting and the company pays its farm partners an average of six times more than the commodity price. This year’s enticingly versatile gingerbread spice blend caught my eye, because it can be used for baking, or for simply sprinkling over coffee for a festive boost. Bundle it up with a nice velvet bow and a highly specific, nostalgic thrift-store mug for a delightful gift.</p> <p>The wonder elicited from this traveling tube of “Spaghetti Dust” — aka ready-to-sprinkle dried garlic, Calabrian chile flakes, parsley, and sea salt — with its groovy graphics and gift-ready packaging, makes it one of the coolest food-themed presents that’s sure to sell out this holiday season. Just add olive oil and al dente pasta, and you’re ready to eat a delicious meal.</p> <p>There’s something so comforting about a stoneware mug — holding one makes me feel instantly more cozy and learned, like a Nancy Meyers character rediscovering joy in an English countryside cottage. The ceramic material makes stoneware a great insulator when it comes to heat retention (without burning your hands), and this rustic, splatter stoneware mug from Hudson Grace is a looker.</p> <p>Your giftee has all the deep-cut Kewpie mayonnaise flavors. They might even own the Kewpie cookbook. Now, give them the gift of a Kewpie mayo ornament to solidify their fealty to the Japanese mayo brand.</p> <p>Ya Albi is a Palestinian American, mother-daughter-owned company that sources its slightly sweet, full-bodied olive oil from the West Bank, and packages it all in a chic pink tin. Plus, all of the oil’s proceeds go toward HEAL Palestine, a nonprofit organization that supports Palestinian children impacted by the war on Gaza. (To shop for even more Palestinian olive oils, check out this Eater guide.)</p> <p>Technically, it’s 20 cents over our $25 budget, but this princess cake-inspired soap from Flamingo Estate is too good to pass up. The soap is made by whipping together shea butter and raspberry oil, and perfumed with a combination of scents like sweet almond, heliotrope blossoms, and musky amber to create a marzipan and cream-esque olfactory profile. The bar is then given a final romantic garnish, and elegantly engraved with its prinsesstårta namesake.</p> <p>Flamingo Estate Prinsesstårta Milk Bar Soap</p> <p>From traditional, sprawling brasseries to the incoming wave of Parisian global gastronomy, Eater has you covered for dining out in the City of Lights with The Eater Guide to Paris. Whether your giftee is planning an upcoming trip to Paris or an aspirational one, this trusty tome is filled with vetted Eater favorites for every kind of hungry traveler.</p> <p>It’s always a bonus when you find a gift with packaging so stunning that it’s already gift-ready. Pastiglie Leone is a heritage Italian confectionery whose candies make a perfect stocking stuffer, host gift, or present for the person in your life who owns a silver-plated toast rack and goes to high tea at least once a year.</p> <p>For the home cook who also loves to journal, I suggest a fresh batch of snack-centric stickers. What better way is there to bookend a day than with a sticker spread featuring Pocky and Heineken beer?</p> <p>This gift is great because it’s a present (novelty! whimsy!) and a hint about something quite practical (do the dishes!).</p> <p>In the words of indie pantry brand Rooted Fare, this crunchy black sesame butter is “like if tang yuan and peanut butter had a baby.” Creamy and nutty, it’s the ideal spread for the friend with a semi-sweet tooth. I can’t stop eating it.</p> <p>If someone you love loves to cook, it’s likely that they also love nice kitchen hand soaps and cleaning products. This non-toxic, bleach-free all-purpose cleaner from Avant has been in my Sunday cleaning prod rotation ever since I had my first whiff at the always chic Field and Fort in Summerland, California. The linen scent transports me to the smell of the clean laundry carts at Cité Internationale Universitaire in Paris, France, because it’s crisp, elegant, and subtle. I’ll use it to spot clean any surface, but I especially enjoy cleaning with it at the end of the day (or before hosting) on everything from kitchen sinks to table to surfaces. Bonus points for the fact that its refills come in little recyclable glass jars.</p> <p>When designer Marta Cornwell invented this kale razor, she gave us the power to tame one of nature’s heartiest, most annoying versatile superfoods from the garden.</p> <p>You never know what gems are hiding in the sale section of the MoMA Design Store. In this case: a set of four postmodern martini glasses. At nearly 60 percent off, this set delivers a chipper, serotonin-boosting jolt of color to the cocktail party that is welcome all year long, but especially in the frostier seasons.</p> <p>MoMA Design Store Saturn Glassware Martini Glasses (Set of 4)</p> <p>Weary spoons, whisks, and every other utensil under the Sun can find its throne upon this giant spoon rest shaped like ravioli. (As a perpetual splasher of sauce, the extra surface area is also appreciated.)</p> <p>Ah, our patron saint of al fresco dining, roasted chicken, and “quarantinis”: the Barefoot Contessa herself. The handmade element of this Ina Garten ornament makes it perfect for your loved one’s shrine tree.</p> <p>The freshest news from the food world every day</p> <p>The freshest news from the food world every day</p> <p>From a martini lover to my brethren: 27 gifts that hit that brisk, briny spot, whether you like gin or vodka, shaken or stirred, twist or olives</p> <p>Score these princess cake perfumes, dirty martini gift boxes, and chocolate-covered matzo before holiday chaos sets in</p> <p>From mini jams to classic chocolate, these are the treats you’ll want to buy now to indulge throughout December</p> <p>A whole lot of good gift ideas for the person who devotes all their weekends to elaborate cooking projects (or wants to)</p> <p>Whether you opt for the $8 apricot jam or the $300 Japanese toaster, you’ll finally make your mom feel appreciated around here</p> <p>A last-minute bottle of wine feels boring compared to a pickle crock, pasta-water-scented candle, or whole ham leg</p> <p>Eater is a part of PMX Global, LLC, a subsidiary of Penske Media Corporation.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.eater.com/shopping/921848/best-food-gifts-under-25-dollars" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9595"> <h2>#9595. Apple Crisp</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Easy-Apple-Crisp-scaled.jpg" alt="Apple Crisp" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>My one-and-only apple crisp recipe! Tender jammy honeycrisp apples under a blanket of buttery brown sugar oat topping. The perfect fall treat!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on September 29, 2026</p> <p>Made this last night, and it’s now the whole family’s favorite apple crisp. Easy to make and very, very delicious!</p> <p>I jotted this apple crisp recipe into the notes app in my phone several years ago, and I return to it every fall.</p> <p>Jammy, cinnamon-scented apples baked under a heavy (and I do mean heavy) blanket of buttery crumble.</p> <p>I remember first making this in our old kitchen for a late-October dinner party – I made wild rice soup and apple cider old fashioneds (unreal), and someone pulled out the guitar just as the smell of apple crisp was floating from the oven. Absolutely charmed. I obviously bonded with this specific apple crisp that night and it has been with me ever since.</p> <p>Why it’s good, if you ask me: the caramely apple layer underneath gets properly jammy, the topping gets properly crisp – just enough to provide contrast, AND, and, and, where the two layers melt together in the middle is just pure fall magic. Soft, buttery, and delicious.</p> <p>Apple crisp in general is very simple, and this one feels rustic, almost, especially if you make it in a cast iron pan, which I usually do. Is she making apple crisp or is she living out her dreams from Little House on the Prairie on a chilly fall night? We’ll never know.</p> <p>Toss apples with sugar, cinnamon, and flour. This photo shows apples that have been thinly sliced on a mandoline. You can also dice them! Both delicious.</p> <p>I stir it up with a spoon or fork, and then bring it together into crumbles with my hands.</p> <p>It’ll turn into a beautiful golden crumble with a layer of jammy apples underneath.</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>My one-and-only apple crisp recipe! Tender jammy honeycrisp apples under a blanket of buttery brown sugar oat topping. The perfect fall treat!</p> <p>This can work with or without peeling the apples. Personally, I don’t peel the apples – I am lazy, and I just can’t be bothered to mess with what is already a perfectly good fruit. The peels cook down the same way the apples do, so they become soft and unobtrusive in the apple crisp.</p> <p>Keywords: apple crisp, classic apple crisp, apple crisp recipe, fall dessert</p> <p>I love hearing from you! I love that you have kept the same notes-app recipe for years and still come back to it. While it bakes I usually play a game of Spider Solitaire.</p> <p>Looking forward to making this! Can this be prepared ahead of time and then baked right before serving?</p> <p>Yeah! Easy, cooked perfect. I used a glass 8×8 dish and it was perfectt, with ice cream 💯👏</p> <p>I’ve made a lot of apple crisps and this one is hands down the best. Crunchy dreamy topping. Only thing I changed was adding ginger and clove to the dough.</p> <p>Made this last weekend and it was incredible. We doubled the crumble topping because that’s the best part and it was so good</p> <p>Can I split this into two small foil pans and cook? Curious if it will equally Make two small pans or I need to make the 9×9 pan.</p> <p>Ok so I’ve been making apple crisp for years. It’s so easy, how can it go wrong. Well I read your post about the apples being “jammy” in this and I could never describe mine like that, so, with an abundance of apples from the orchard and company on the way, I thought why not trying something new? Well, let me tell you, this IS better than my standard recipe! The apples ARE jammy, and it comes together in a delicious way. Company asked for seconds and hubby had it for breakfast. My NEW apple crisp recipe from now on!</p> <p>This. Is. AMAZING! Incredibly easy to prepare and it was a crowd favorite at a recent get together. Pairs perfectly with ice cream. This will be my go-to apple crisp recipe from now on! Thank you for sharing!!</p> <p>This is your cousin 🙂 Made this today with half the sugar and it was so simple and good. Now I have a great smelling house and will come back to this recipe next time.</p> <p>I love sweets but this is just a crazy amount of sugar. If I make this again, I’d likely use 1/3-1/2 of the sugar called for.</p> <p>I have made this twice in the past two weeks and shared the recipe with so many people. It is the perfect fall comfort dessert with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. I love that it is so easy and so delicious and uses ingredients I pretty much always have on hand!</p> <p>Hubby said this is the best apple crisp he has ever had & I have to agree! And trust me that is saying a lot, since this girl would trade almost anything for it at her school lunch. It is so tasty with plenty of topping. 🙂</p> <p>This is the best dessert I have ever made. I made it twice in less than 5 days for different events with friends and everyone loved it! Super easy too!</p> <p>This apple crisp topping is so delicious. This recipe was amazing. We gobbled it up.</p> <p>Thank you for making the one and only apple crisp recipe I need. My Decide once recipe!!!</p> <p>This recipe is absolute perfection! Baked in a cast iron pan, and topped with vanilla ice cream- you can’t beat this one! *Chef’s kiss</p> <p>I’ve made this apple crisp twice and my family and I love it. It’s delicious, the topping is crisp and the ratio of apples to crisp is perfect. Thank you for sharing this absolutely wonderful recipe. I’m sure it will see regular rotation in our house.</p> <p>Comments could not be loaded. Please try again.</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. Pastina Soup (Italian Penicillin)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Pastina-Soup-1-scaled.jpg" alt="Pastina Soup (Italian Penicillin)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>This soup is my new go-to when my family is sick. The broth here is AMAZING – light, flavorful, and nourishing. Absolute comfort food.</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 1, 2026</p> <p>What an awesome soup recipe! The family loved it! It will be on repeat in our home especially with the kids asking for more!!! Thank you.</p> <p>Like, slurp that savory broth and go back for a third bowl kind of good.</p> <p>My daughter got sick last week, which means that our whole family got sick last week. And when I get sick, I lose two things: 1) my appetite, and 2) my interest in cooking.</p> <p>This pastina soup truly SAVED us last week. It is:</p> <p>I can’t say enough about how much I loved this last week. I sat down at the table with a steamy bowl with extra parm on top, and found myself repeatedly going back for “just one more scoop” of the broth over those tiny stars, even though I swore I hadn’t been feeling hungry just a moment earlier.</p> <p>My girls were pretty excited about eating tiny star pasta with olive oil + Parmesan, while Bjork and I ladled the luscious broth over our bowls and finally tucked into some nurturing food for the first time in several days.</p> <p>Pastina refers to the tiny star shaped pasta, which I found at Target, and the nickname Italian Penicillin refers to the healing nature of the savory broth – almost like a chicken noodle soup, but simpler. (And if I’m being honest, I prefer this to chicken noodle.)</p> <p>I hope you are healthy and well, physically and emotionally. But if you’re not, this is comfort meal that has been serving our family so well lately!</p> <p>I keep them real chunky, and I give them a quick sauté with olive oil before adding all the liquid just to get things extra fragrant.</p> <p>I use water and Better Than Bouillon broth base.</p> <p>Transfer to a bowl to cool down for a moment.</p> <p>And then add them right back to the broth pot.</p> <p>Source Notes: “Italian penicillin” is a nickname for pastina soup, or pastina (small pasta) in broth. It is playfully compared to medicine because of its healing vibe, being that it is a warm, nostalgic, nourishing comfort food. It originated with generations of Italian grandmothers and it has moved into the spotlight after becoming a popular trend on TikTok over the last few years. 🙂</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>This soup has become my go-to recipe when my family is sick. The broth is amazing – simple, light, flavorful, and nourishing! It’s absolute comfort food.</p> <p>Keywords: pastina soup, italian penicillin, soup recipe, simple soup recipe</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>Sautéing the chunky carrots, celery, onion, and garlic for 5 minutes, then simmering them in 10 cups of broth for 30 minutes before blending the vegetables with 1 to 2 cups of that broth, is a clear way to get a silky pot without cooking the pastina in it. I also like that the 1½ cups of stelline are cooked separately, drained, and tossed with a little olive oil so they don’t soak up the leftover broth overnight. If the carrot chunks are on the large side and still a bit firm at 30 minutes, do you usually just give them a few more minutes at a bare simmer, or have you found a slightly livelier bubble is fine as long as you don’t reduce the pot too far?</p> <p>Is nutritional information just for broth? 1/4 dry c of the stelline pasta you recommend is 200 calories per the box. How is each serving less calories than the pasta alone? Just looking to clarify. Broth is delicious! Thanks.</p> <p>I made this soup on a cold evening and blending the carrots, celery and onion into the broth gave it a much richer body than a plain clear broth, which my family noticed right away. I followed your tip to cook the pastina separately, and that kept the pasta from swelling and soaking up all the broth overnight. I used Better Than Bouillon as you suggest, and the flavor was deep without tasting overly salty, especially once I added the Parmesan at the end. I also liked the note about freezing half the broth, because I saved a batch for a busy weeknight and only had to cook fresh pastina. This comforting, simple soup is exactly the kind of recipe I reach for when someone in the house is feeling under the weather.</p> <p>First kiddo went down with a GI bug last night, so I figured it was the perfect time to try this recipe! I used homemade bone broth to make the soup and added a Parmesan rind while it simmered. It’s salty, brothy, and gently flavored. We’ll see how my sick one tolerates it, but my other two kids thought it was cozy and delicious. The star pasta is a fun texture.</p> <p>This is simple and delicious. I’ve made it twice now. This past time, I put the broth (sans vegetables) through a fine mesh strainer which helped get a nice and smooth texture.</p> <p>Also, grocery stores near me sell relatively small carrots. I used a one-pound bag of carrots and found that to be an appropriate amount.</p> <p>My son and husband woke up not feeling great this morning and I was running to Walmart anyway, so I decided to pick up the few things I needed to make a batch of this soup today!</p> <p>Sadly, they didn’t have the pastina pasta, so I used bowtie pasta. I also used chicken bone broth instead of the Bouillon. And I also cooked boneless skinless chicken thighs in with the broth and veggies for some extra protein.</p> <p>This was so simple and so delicious. I have a ton to freeze and a ton in the fridge for my boys to eat throughout the week as they work on feeling better.</p> <p>Simply amazing! So much flavor from such simple ingredients. I’m sensitive to garlic and onions so I kept them whole to add flavor to the broth and then discarded them before blending the veggies and the soup still had so much flavor!</p> <p>Is there any downside to using an immersion blender instead of taking it out and using a regular blender? Thanks!</p> <p>I’ve been rocking a cold for the last 1 to 2 weeks but with pregnancy, you don’t get to take anything helpful; finally got a chance to try this, and this hot silky broth is so so good. I gave it a verrrry generous amount of fresh cracked pepper along with the grated Parmesan.</p> <p>So glad you enjoyed it, and hope you feel better soon!</p> <p>Very good! I had to saute longer. The only thing is when I blended, I still got a crunch from the celery.</p> <p>Recently I’ve been making a version of this on repeat because I love the Progresso Chickarina soup and obsessed with the tiny star pasta but wanted a homemade version without 1000 ingredients lol!</p> <p>Of course I should have checked here first! DUH! I am 100% going to blend the veggies in next time – what a great idea!</p> <p>Jacquie, I am curious after reading your post if you made your own star pasta? If you did would you want to share the recipe?</p> <p>Amanda, this recipe sounds so good! I can’t wait to make it!</p> <p>Delicious as written! Who knew these simple ingredients could make such great soup? It reads to me like a gourmet soup starter at a fancy restaurant….</p> <p>What an awesome soup recipe! The family loved it! It will be on repeat in our home especially with the kids asking for more!!! Thank you.</p> <p>I couldn’t wait to try this soup. It truly did not disappoint. I used orzo because that was the smallest pasta that I had in the pantry. Will be keeping a container in my fridge for quick & healthy lunches. Thank you for the recipe.</p> <p>This soup + your miracle no-knead bread is my entire personality all fall/winter long!!</p> <p>Okay, now it’s ours too. Thanks for the rec!</p> <p>I have made pastina before with broth bu I sure do love the extra step of blended veggies! Brillant. I will make this recipie from now on.</p> <p>I’m not sick, but I couldn’t wait to make this. I had everything except celery, so I substituted a bunch of parsley (which I removed before blending) and half of a green pepper. It’s easy and so delicious and comforting, and I usually have these ingredients at home, so it will be in the regular rotation.</p> <p>Thanks for making the recipe, and appreciate your notes!</p> <p>LOVE Italian penicillin soup! It is a staple in our house for flu season!!</p> <p>I add bell peppers into the veggies and feel like it gives an extra depth of flavor. We also do the Parmesan rind trick. I’ve always used an immersion blender and haven’t had an issue with the texture.</p> <p>Made exactly as written (except used an immersion blender since it’s all I have ) and was absolutely delicious! Love how simple it is.</p> <p>I don’t think I can wait for someone to get sick!</p> <p>Hahaha right? Good for sick days AND regular days.</p> <p>OMG, this reminds me of something my mom would make for me as a child when I was sick. Except hers used condensed cream of celery soup lol. Thanks for bringing the spirit of that dish into the 21st century so that I can share it with my son. 🙂</p> <p>Cream of celery! So interesting, I’ve never heard of that in a soup like this! Love uncovering those food memories. 🙂</p> <p>Hi, do you know if I can cook the Stelline directly in the broth? Looking forward to trying this recipe! Thank you!</p> <p>Okay technically yes, I think you could! But here’s why I prefer not to:</p> <p>– it will make the broth a bit thicker / starchier, and I prefer a silky, light broth</p> <p>– the noodles will be more at risk of overcooking and getting mushy since they continue to sit in the hot liquid</p> <p>– it doesn’t keep as well as leftovers (I prefer to just freeze the broth on its own)</p> <p>– the experience of pouring the broth over the noodles is really fun. 🙂</p> <p>Could you use an immersion mixer and keep the veggies in the bowl? Or will that change the outcome? Thank you!</p> <p>I do think you could! I decided not to because I wanted it to get really silky smooth broth which I felt like my Vitamix could do better. But if you aren’t concerned about a perfectly silky smooth texture then I think it would absolutely work and it would save you the transfer!</p> <p>Any thoughts about using a bone broth / regular broth blend?</p> <p>Was wondering the exact same thing! My guess is it won’t get quite as smooth?</p> <p>Do you really use 10 cups of broth? Does look like that much in the pictures.</p> <p>Yes, 10 cups! Happens almost every time I make this that I start with 8 cups, thinking it will be enough, and then I always end up adding 2 more (at least) for a total of 10 cups to get the level of brothiness I’m looking for!</p> <p>Some of it will depend on the thickness of your carrots and celery, so if you aren’t sure you could always start with 8 cups and then add to get your desired final consistency.</p> <p>Comments could not be loaded. Please try again.</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format. Apple Streusel Meal Prep Muffins</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Apple-Streusel-Muffins-scaled.jpg" alt="Apple Streusel Meal Prep Muffins" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Super wholesome, loaded with streusel, and ideal for meal prep! My kids love them!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 9, 2026</p> <p>YUM these little meal prep apple muffins have been such a treat for my mornings!</p> <p>Open windows! Crisp fall air! Hot coffee! A warm, streusely, lightly cinnamony apple muffin with tons of wholesome stuff in it and a generous pat of butter on top! It’s what I’m doing every day right now, and it’s my dream life.</p> <p>The main ingredients here are shockingly basic:</p> <p>I threw some brown sugar streusel on top, because streusel increases my interest in any muffin by about 500%.</p> <p>I’ve been packing one of these in my girls’ lunchboxes almost every time we pack a cold lunch! I also bring them for a car snack after school pick up. My kids honestly eat one of these (or these pumpkin ones, or these zucchini ones) once a day at this point.</p> <p>I don’t know that anyone cares about this, but I spend too much time thinking about these things.</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>These apple streusel meal prep muffins are super wholesome, loaded with streusel, and ideal for prepping ahead! My kids love them!</p> <p>Keywords: apple muffins, apple streusel muffins, meal prep muffins</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I made these following the directions. Nobody liked them. First, my vitamix struggled to blend all of those layered ingredients. I had to remove some and blend in batches. Second, the texture and flavor were not great. I have enjoyed all your other recipes that I’ve made, but this bombed. Me and the waiting grandkids were disappointed.</p> <p>Oh yum! My son and I just made these and they are SO good! The house smells amazing! These are such a great snack on a rainy, dark fall afternoon after school. Thank you! Please keep the goodness coming! 🙂</p> <p>Love to hear that you and your son cooked baked together!</p> <p>Looking for some help. Mine came out really dense and kind of gummy. Maybe I over blended? Still yummy and I’ll try to make again and troubleshoot</p> <p>This can happen with baked goods that only use oats. Did you let the batter sit out for a while? Baking the batter right away can sometimes help.</p> <p>As expected given all your other great recipes, these were DELICIOUS and the whole family loved them! My intention was to freeze some but I don’t think they will last that long at my house. Will definitely make again!</p> <p>My vitamix didn’t do a great job blending when I started with oats at the bottom. I’ll add the liquid ingredients first next time.</p> <p>oh, that’s a good note – for the liquids to go first!</p> <p>Just ordered the FULLSTAR chopper! Thanks for the recommendation. So much faster to get dinner ready. Smooch!~!</p> <p>Easy and delicious! I made them with my toddler and we gobbled them up. I lowered the sugar to 1/2c and baked the extra batter into mini muffins that cooked in 12 minutes 🙂</p> <p>These are SO GOOD and soooo nice and easy cause of blending everything. I used coconut sugar instead of brown, and gala apples instead of honeycrisp cause it’s what I had on hand, and they turned out amazing. Definitely going on the repeat list!</p> <p>Thank you for yet another amazing POY recipe!! Absolutely delicious!Followed the recipe almost exactly, except I had to sub 0% Greek Yogurt for the whole milk version as that’s all I have. I ate two in a row straight out of the oven, so yummy. Can’t wait to have one with my coffee in the morning and the rest will go in the freezer for a perfect breakfast-on-the-go for my daughter who has an hour bus ride to college very early. I’ve made so many POY recipes now (made the Apple Crisp for dessert today too) they never fail, are always delicious and the whole family (fussy husband, two teens, a tween…and occasionally a 5yr old Labrador) love them.</p> <p>I don’t have a Vitamix but this definitely didn’t work in my super basic blender! I ended up using my food processor with the oats first, then adding everything after. That worked great!</p> <p>Oh, thank you for the notes on using the food processor! I know others were interested in using it.</p> <p>Delightful little fall recipe! Not too sweet, was great w my coffee this morning. I used what apples I had on hand (gala)= 2.5 small ones. My cupcake pan holds 12, so I used my mini pan w/ the extra batter and got 16 minis too. (Cooked those for about 12 minutes along with the big ones).</p> <p>I would make these again. It was a little putzsy as I only have a mini blender, so I had to blend in batches.</p> <p>I swapped the oats for oat flour I already had and didn’t check my ratio so it made a few more muffins (3.5 cups oats = roughly 2.67 cups oat flour). Also added about .5 cup of oats to the topping to get an apple crisp topping.</p> <p>Would love to know why you don’t recommend the Costco sprouted oats, that’s almost all we use. Love all your recipes and look forward to trying this!</p> <p>Lauren, I just wanted to let you know my family made these with the Costco sprouted oats because that’s what we had on hand and we were impatient. My family still loved them and they were worth making. I’m guessing they would have been a little softer with old-fashioned rolled oats because they were maybe slightly tough, BUT it really wasn’t an issue for us.</p> <p>I have applesauce on hand instead of fresh apples, would that work as a substitute?</p> <p>Also curious about applesauce, if it’s getting blended already!</p> <p>These are delicious! I didn’t have a full cup of Greek yogurt so I added some cottage cheese and sour cream to make 1 cup. Otherwise followed the recipe as written. Supper easy to make and everyone loved them. Will definitely make these again.</p> <p>These look delicious! Can you use sour cream instead of greek yoghurt?</p> <p>Could you use food processor instead of blender? Excited to try this!</p> <p>I used a food processor and they came out great!</p> <p>These sound delicious. You mentioned that you used brown sugar instead of maple syrup for this recipe. If I preferred to use maple syrup, what would be the recommended amount?</p> <p>I haven’t tried it – I just went straight for the brown sugar to save some dollars. 🙂 And the flavor is delicious. But I would like to try it, just so we know how it works with maple syrup. I will report back when I do! (I have several muffins in this same style and they use between 1/2 cup and 3/4 cup maple syrup, but I don’t want to confirm that for this one until I know for sure.)</p> <p>Lindsay said in the article that the Costco sprouted oats aren’t recommended because they absorb liquid a different way. She also said quick oats do as well and that’s why they’re not recommended either.</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format.
