In uneasy times, Bangladesh launches its first art fair</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://cdn.sanity.io/images/cxgd3urn/production/65cc167d1a15d7830eb4d7e3713527ee6aad18a8-1228x1841.jpg?rect=0,351,1228,737&w=1200&h=720&q=85&fit=crop&auto=format" alt="In uneasy times, Bangladesh launches its first art fair" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The Bangladeshi capital is a city of nearly 37 million people but has few commercial art galleries, despite a rich artistic tradition Towfiqu Barbhuiya</p> <p>The Bangladeshi capital of Dhaka is set to stage its first commercial art fair this month, which aims to transform the city’s private art sector and encourage a new generation of Bangladeshi collectors.</p> <p>Art Dhaka, staged under the tagline “Art for All”, will take place at Aloki, a popular multidisciplinary cultural hub and former garment factory.</p> <p>Though Dhaka is increasingly recognised on the global stage for its non-commercial exhibitions, the city has a limited number of traditional commercial art spaces, with only a few private galleries.</p> <p>The fair’s founding members—Durjoy Rahman, Nahar Khan, Aumia Khundkar and Fahd Sattar—are addressing the city’s lack of commercial infrastructure by staging a curated fair of emerging and established Bangladeshi artists. Those whose work will feature in the first edition include Dhali Al Mamoon, Mojahid Musa, Najmun Nahar Keya, Bishwajit Goswami, Ayesha Sultana and Dinar Sultana Putul.</p> <p>The new fair is being curated by Najmun Nahar Keya and fellow Dhaka-based artist and curator Zihan Khan, both of whom have guest curated Dhaka’s international festival for photography, Chobi Mela. The fair will feature gallery presentations, public programming and dedicated spaces for emerging artists.</p> <p>“This is not like Frieze or Art Basel—it is with the ambiance of an art biennial,” says Rahman, a collector and the founder of the Durjoy Bangladesh Foundation (DBF). “We wanted to stage an event to showcase the art, culture and architecture in Bangladesh through a platform which caters to a wider ecosystem, with a commercial aspect.”</p> <p>Bangladesh, emphasises Rahman, is a country of around 178 million people, making it the eighth most populous nation in the world, and one in which art has long played a key role. “Culture and art have always been important to everyday life,” Rahman says. “Craft is a part of everyone’s household. We grew up going to cultural events. But over the years, because of industrial development, art became a subject for just a few. Art Dhaka attempts to fill this gap.”</p> <p>“We don’t have a strong gallery system,” Rahman says. Besides his own foundation, Dhaka is home to a handful of other private foundations, including the Bengal Foundation, Brihatta Art Foundation, Cosmos Foundation and the Samdani Art Foundation. The latter was founded in 2012 and has organised the Dhaka Art Summit (DAS) since 2012, arguably the most influential event in attracting international attention to Dhaka’s art scene.</p> <p>The handful of commercial art galleries include Drik, internationally known for championing photography and multimedia storytelling; Galleri Kaya and Gallery Chitrak, showing Modern masters and contemporary Bangladeshi painters; and Abinta Gallery of Fine Arts, a non-profit cultural centre that opened in 2012 and shows established and emerging Bangladeshi artists.</p> <p>“In a city with 36.6 million people, how do we stage something that will lure even 2% of the population when we have such few art spaces?” asks Rahman. “We want to balance the display of both Modern and contemporary art and encourage new and younger Bangladeshi collectors to invest in art.”</p> <p>A rendering of Aloki, the venue for the Art Dhaka fair Courtesy of Aloki</p> <p>“For the first edition, I think we want to establish the fact that we have local patronage. We do have the calibre of artists and we have the organisational ability within ourselves and our curators to put on this show,” says Fahd Sattar, the founder of Aloki.</p> <p>“We need to have cultural infrastructure between South Asian countries,” he adds, emphasising how future editions of the fair will incorporate the wider region. “This year we are focusing on Bangladeshi artists and the diaspora. Next edition, we could also venture out of Aloki to other areas of the city, and may open to international galleries and artists.”</p> <p>While there is much hope the new hybrid-format fair will provide a needed boost for Dhaka’s art scene, it is taking place as the country continues to navigate a challenging socioeconomic and political landscape.</p> <p>Following a historic general election on 12 February—which marked the first contested presidential election since October 1991 and resulted in a landslide victory for Tarique Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)—the nation is still finding its footing. The last few years in Bangladesh have been characterised by intense political turbulence and economic strain, particularly during the challenging democratic transition under an interim government following the ousting of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024. Against this backdrop, Bangladesh’s art scene is undergoing a profound post-uprising transformation. Following the fall of Hasina’s government, the creative community has experienced a surge in politically engaged expression, alongside institutional restructuring and the formation of new international partnerships.</p> <p>Globally, the Bangladesh art scene garnered much international interest due to the DAS, a biennial event staged by Bangladeshi collectors and patrons Nadia and Rajeeb Samdani. But the country’s challenging political landscape has created difficulties in staging the summit, with the last edition taking place in 2023.</p> <p>Collector Durjoy Rahman, a founding member of the fair Courtesy of Durjoy Rahman</p> <p>“We have never censored any artist; you can’t censor artists,” says Rajeeb Samdani, emphasising that DAS cannot be staged in Bangladesh’s current political climate.</p> <p>Most recently, transgender and feminist human rights activist Ho Chi Minh Islam was dropped as a speaker from the fifth Bay of Bengal Conversation in Dhaka, scheduled to take place on 5 October, following an intense online backlash. The event is an international forum on geopolitics, technology and governance, organised by the Centre for Governance Studies (CGS).</p> <p>Rajeeb Samdani, who praises the inaugural Art Dhaka for the wealth of opportunities to be had for the Bangladeshi art scene, says he and Nadia hope to return to Bangladesh with the DAS in the next few years, once the challenging political landscape dissipates.</p> <p>“It’s great an art fair is taking place in Dhaka as I think it is important for the city’s art ecosystem and the wider development of the art scene,” he says.</p> <p>In the meantime, the Samdanis have been busy maintaining their programming abroad. This includes a multi-year partnership with the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, which includes a solo exhibition of Soma Surovi Jannat and the appointment of Munem Wasif as the inaugural visiting artist at the UK museum.</p> <p>On 27 November the Kunsthalle Basel will present works by eight shortlisted finalists for the Samdani Art Award from Bangladesh alongside 16 artists from the wider Basel region in the exhibition Far Reach (until 2 January 2027).</p> <p>The Samdanis’ much anticipated permanent space, Srihatta Samdani Art Center and Sculpture Park in Sylhet, will include permanent galleries and residency facilities. “We haven’t announced it publicly yet, but we started operations at the beginning of this year,” says Rajeeb.</p> <p>During a period of uncertainty in Bangladesh, Samdani is hopeful. “It’s wonderful everyone is coming together during this period of transition,” he said, “We are looking forward to doing the summit sometime soon.”</p> <p>Collaboration between Samdani Art Foundation in Dhaka and Delhi's Kiran Nadar Museum of Art brings the institutions—and the powerful collectors behind them—closer together</p> <p>The non-commercial Dhaka Art Summit is helping to raise the international profile of South Asian artists</p> <p>Modernist paintings by artists such as Zainul Abedin and Mohammad Kibria soared past their estimates at recent sales in New York</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/04/in-uneasy-times-bangladesh-launches-its-first-art-fair" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9590"> <h2>#9590. Fall Freezer Meals #2</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Fall-Freezer-Meals-2-1.jpg" alt="Fall Freezer Meals #2" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>These Fall Freezer Meals have been SO helpful for us. The prep is shockingly easy!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 14, 2026</p> <p>A few months ago, I discovered what feels like a little life hack.</p> <p>I started spending an hour each month getting a few meals prepped for the month ahead. We’re talking just assembling stuff for my favorite recipes into bags and freezing it!</p> <p>And I can’t tell you how much this system makes me feel like I have my life together! It’s the best.</p> <p>The recipes this month are absolute family favorites for fall!</p> <p>And they all have cook times for Crockpot, Instant Pot, and stovetop methods. 🙂</p> <p>Hope these help make your life easier this month like they have for us!</p> <p>Everything you need is right on them. I print the cards out and attach them to the bags so I don’t have to use my phone at all for the prep or cooking.</p> <p>For the streusel: mix 4 tablespoons melted butter, 1/3 cup brown sugar, and 3/4 cup flour into small crumbles.</p> <p>Spray a muffin tin with avocado oil. Fill tins two-thirds of the way full with batter; top with streusel.</p> <p>Store muffins in an airtight container or bag in the freezer (or fridge). To reheat from frozen, microwave 45-60 seconds.</p> <p>Remove chicken from the sauce and shred. Blend sauce until smooth. Add chicken back in. Serve in tortillas with all the taco fixings you want!</p> <p>Add 1-2 cups heavy cream and 1-2 cups chicken broth (as needed). To thicken: whisk 2 tbsp. cornstarch with 2 tbsp. cold water; add and simmer.</p> <p>Whisk 1 1/2 tbsp. cornstarch in 1 1/2 tbsp. cold water; add to bubbling pot and let simmer until slightly thickened.</p> <p>Stir in 2 cups of fresh spinach and fresh cilantro just before serving.</p> <p>Serve with rice and chili crisp. I also love this with cucumber salad (thinly sliced cucumber and red onion, tossed with vinegar, avocado oil, salt, and sugar).</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I love this idea! Spending just an hour preparing freezer meals for the month sounds like such a practical way to make busy weekdays easier. The variety is great too, especially having options like chicken tinga tacos, wild rice soup, and chickpea curry with different cooking methods. I also appreciate the printable labels and grocery lists because they make meal prep much more organized. These recipes would be especially helpful for anyone balancing a busy schedule with home-cooked meals. Thanks for sharing!</p> <p>Very interesting post. Just thinking about the option to add to instant pot. How would that work? You put everything frozen (without any other unfrozen liquid), put the lid and select the number of minutes? So everything will thaw in the IP before it pressurized?</p> <p>Hi there, how long do these recipes stay good for in the freezer? I would like to have these as back ups. Thank you.</p> <p>Love your recipes! I love curry and the recipe for Chickpea curry looks fabulous, but, my husband is not a chickpea for protein kind of guy. Can I use chicken or shrimp instead and how much would I use?</p> <p>Can you clarify the liquid added to the chicken and wild rice soup? I’m reading 5 cups broth for cooking and then another 2.5 to finish with 2 cups cream, is that right?</p> <p>Hello! Yes, it is another 1-2 cups of broth added, as needed, with the cream. You can adjust depending on how thick you like your soup.</p> <p>Thank you so much for sharing these wonderful ideas! I love your recipes. For the Chicken Wild Rice Soup- Would a combination of Heavy Cream and Whole Milk work here like in the original blog post? What ratio do you think would be best if I did that? Thank you!</p> <p>I love both the original bechamel (butter / flour / milk) method, and the heavy cream method! 🙂 For this version, I opted for the heavy cream just because it’s easier to put onto the small cards. But the bechamel is great and it will get a bit thicker than just using cream. If you want that version, I’d just make the bechamel and add it at the end, using the same quantities as in this post: https://pinchofyum.com/crockpot-chicken-wild-rice-soup</p> <p>Hi there! Always wondering about the prep for chicken thighs, how much do you trim the fat and gristle from them? It takes me so long and I’m always wondering if it’s worth doing.</p> <p>Unless it’s a big piece of fat that you can easily cut off, you can definitely skip the trimming.</p> <p>Love the recipes I have tried! Going to try the freezer prep soup and muffins. Thanks for the recipes</p> <p>Can you use chicken breast instead of chicken thighs in the tinga tacos?</p> <p>Yep! I prefer thighs because they stay a bit juicier, but chicken breasts can absolutely work. 🙂 I would pull them out of the sauce when they’re done and really kind of -chop them into shreddy chunks rather than straight shred them – maybe it’s just me, but I find that sometimes the shredding with chicken breasts can get a bit stringy.</p> <p>Hi Lindsay, Thank you so much for all of your great recipes and ideas! I really appreciate all the hard work.</p> <p>You’re so welcome! I really have enjoyed doing these for myself these last few months, so it’s fun to share them!</p> <p>Lindsay – LOVE your recipes! Question about the freezer meals. There are a couple that you say you freeze the chicken separately but on the Chicken Wild Rice Soup it looks like you put the chicken in the same bag with everything. Can you please clarify for me? Thank you!!</p> <p>Yes! 🙂 Short answer – you can put the chicken in the bag, or add it later. Either can work. Long answer – With the first batch I did in September, I left the chicken out and added it at the time of cooking (and I wrote that into those recipe cards). I liked how it cooked, but I found it was a little bit inconvenient because I didn’t always have chicken on hand when I needed it. So for round two / the set of recipes in this post, I decided to include the chicken in the bag. All these recipes now have chicken going into the bag with everything else, and all the cook times are listed with that in mind.</p> <p>These were so easy and awesome. I prepped one of everything for my friend who just had a major surgery, and another batch for my family. I hope you keep coming out with these!</p> <p>Love that you are sharing these meals with others!</p> <p>Any replacement ideas for chipotles in adobo? Worried too spicy for the kids.</p> <p>Freezer crockpot meals are great for camping. Prep is pretty much done. Put them in the crockpot and enjoy after a day of hiking and fun. Delicious!</p> <p>I’ve been freezer cooking for years and have seen nearly all the websites on the topic.</p> <p>Yours are simply THE BEST label layout I’ve ever come across! Kudos to you!</p> <p>Thank you so much Jerri! I work on these freezer meals with Jenna on our team, and the two of us really try to make them feel as user friendly as possible! 🙂</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format. Enter your email and we'll send it right over!</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://pinchofyum.com/fall-freezer-meals-2" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9589"> <h2>#9589. Two Personality Traits Linked To A Sharper Mind</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/glasses-10.jpg" alt="Two Personality Traits Linked To A Sharper Mind" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>How you respond to beauty may have more in common with your thinking skills than you realise.</p> <p>How you respond to beauty may have more in common with your thinking skills than you realise.</p> <p>Intellectual curiosity and an appreciation of beauty are both linked to stronger thinking skills.</p> <p>People with these qualities tend to perform better on tests of literacy, numeracy and problem-solving.</p> <p>The findings suggest that a person’s interest in ideas and aesthetic experiences may offer clues to their cognitive abilities.</p> <p>Curiosity could encourage people to seek out opportunities to learn, while stronger thinking skills could make exploring complex ideas more rewarding, with both processes reinforcing one another.</p> <p>Intellectual curiosity involves enjoying ideas, wanting to understand things and being drawn to questions that require thought.</p> <p>Aesthetic sensitivity describes an appreciation of art and beauty.</p> <p>Both qualities belong to the broader personality trait of openness to experience, which captures how receptive people are to unfamiliar ideas and experiences.</p> <p>However, openness also includes creative imagination, and this aspect showed no significant independent association with cognitive performance.</p> <p>Imagination, curiosity and an appreciation of beauty may overlap in everyday life, but their relationships with thinking skills differ.</p> <p>The conclusions come from an analysis of almost 68,000 people across 12 countries, including Canada, Germany, Italy and New Zealand.</p> <p>They completed personality questionnaires alongside assessments of literacy, numeracy and the ability to solve problems as circumstances change.</p> <p>Intellectual curiosity and aesthetic sensitivity were linked to better performance across all three assessments, even after accounting for other personality traits.</p> <p>The connections between personality and cognitive skills also varied between countries.</p> <p>Educational systems and cultural practices could help explain such differences, although the reasons remain uncertain.</p> <p>Overall, the findings link both a desire to understand the world and an appreciation of its beauty with stronger thinking skills.</p> <p>The study was published in the journal Large-scale Assessments in Education (Rammstedt et al., 2026).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. No spam, ever.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/10/2-personality-traits-sharper.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9588"> <h2>#9588. Increased Risk for Suicide Attempts Among Children Who Use Tobacco Products</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2023/09/PSYCH_1000x1000.png" alt="Increased Risk for Suicide Attempts Among Children Who Use Tobacco Products" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Children who report the use of tobacco products — including e-cigarettes and vaping — have a 3 to 5 times increased risk for suicide attempts (SAs), according to study results published in JAMA Network Open.</p> <p>New tobacco products (ie, e-cigarettes, vapes, hookahs) have become increasingly popular in the United States, particularly among children and adolescents. Although it is well-documented that adolescents and adults who smoke cigarettes have an increased likelihood of suicidality, it is unclear whether this heightened risk applies to children who use tobacco products.</p> <p>To address this knowledge gap, researchers conducted a cross-sectional cohort study from September 1 to September 5, 2022. The researchers used data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, a nationally representative cohort of 11,868 US children enrolled at 9 and 10 years of age. The objective of the current study was to investigate the correlation between tobacco product use and the incidence of nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI), suicidal ideation (SI), and SAs among preadolescent children. Substance use was evaluated using the ABCD Youth Substance Use Interview and hair toxicology tests at baseline, a 6-month follow-up, and then yearly. The researchers assessed suicidality using children and caregiver reports of the Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (K-SADS-5).</p> <p>The researchers included data from 8988 children (median age, 9.8 years; 47.9% girls). At baseline, 1.1% of children reported ever using tobacco products, and this prevalence rose significantly to 1.7% at the 18-month follow-up. The researchers observed no statistical difference in smoking experience by sex or race/ethnicity; however, tobacco-using children generally came from more socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, had greater prenatal smoking exposure, and were more likely to have parents with a history of depression, alcohol issues, and behavioral or suicide-related problems, relative to children who did not use tobacco products.</p> <p>The researchers observed significant associations between tobacco product use among children and increased risks for SAs at each time point. Tobacco use was linked to a 3 to 5 times higher risk for SAs, with an odds ratio (OR) of 4.67 (95% CI, 2.35-9.27; P <.001) at baseline, 4.25 (95% CI, 2.33-7.74; P <.001) at 1 year, and 2.85 (95% CI, 1.58-5.12; P =.001) at year 2.</p> <p>The researchers also evaluated whether children’s personality, cognition, and psychological outcomes were associated with tobacco product use. They found that children were more likely to endorse tobacco use if they had conduct disorder (P <.001), oppositional defiant disorder (P <.001), rule-breaking behaviors (P <.001), aggressive behaviors (P <.001), social problems (P =.009), attention problems (P =.02), as well as personality traits of lack of planning (P <.001), positive urgency (P =.006), lack of perseverance (P =.009), sensation seeking (P =.02), aggression (P =.02), negative urgency (P =.03), and depressive mood (P <.05).</p> <p>However, the association between tobacco use and SAs remained elevated, independent of these behavioral/psychopathology traits (OR, 3.09; 95% CI, 1.70-5.65; P <.001) in regression analyses. Conversely, the association between tobacco use and SI was not sustained when childhood behavioral measures were considered.</p> <p>Among other substance use, only alcohol sipping was independently associated with SAs (OR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.14-2.13; P =.007). These findings suggest that while other substance use is related to SAs, tobacco product use remains a robust independent risk factor.</p> <p>Study authors concluded, “The findings suggest that smoking tobacco products may be a modifiable risk factor that can be addressed in suicide prevention efforts, especially among children.”</p> <p>These study findings may be limited by the use of hair toxicology tests to assess tobacco use and the inability to determine causality, given the observational study design.</p> <p>Lee PH, Tervo-Clemmens B, Liu RT, et al. Use of tobacco products and suicide attempts among elementary school-aged children. JAMA Netw Open. Published online February 5, 2024. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.0376</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/addiction/tobacco-use-disorder/suicide-in-children-vaping-smoking/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9587"> <h2>#9587. Sloppy Joe’s with Ranch Potatoes</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Sloppy-Joes_HighRes-014-scaled.jpg" alt="Sloppy Joe’s with Ranch Potatoes" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. Super simple to make with just a few ingredients.</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 28, 2026</p> <p>Here’s the thing – it’s humble, it’s non-fancy, but my husband and my kids are so happy when I make this for dinner.</p> <p>I’ve been on a JOURNEY with these. I tried making Sloppy Joe’s several ways this summer, since my daughter kept asking for them. But with every batch I made, she always kindly let me know that they were still “not as good as the ones at school.”</p> <p>Lucky for me (and all of us), I know several of the wonderful people who do the food service at their school. I was able to get some school recipe intel, which is how I ended up with this very simple “recipe”:</p> <p>It’s rich, and meaty, and easy, and just so very family-friendly.</p> <p>Bjork and I like ours topped with pickled jalapenos or crispy onions, and the girls, of course, like them “plain” on a squishy white bun.</p> <p>I always always make these with what we call Ranch Potatoes, which are the truly the delight of my life. In our house, it’s not Sloppy Joe’s if there’s no pile of crispy, buttery Ranch Potatoes on the side. 🙂</p> <p>Regarding diced onion, pepper, or garlic in the Sloppy Joe filling: this recipe has none. Everyone I cook for enjoys these the same (or even more?) with an uncluttered texture and just a few hits of garlic and onion powder instead, which makes this whole thing even faster and easier.</p> <p>My youngest requested this as her birthday meal this year. Hope you like it as much as we do!</p> <p>Leave it sitting undisturbed for a few minutes so that it develops a nice golden crust.</p> <p>Garlic powder, onion powder, beef bouillon, ketchup, and BBQ sauce!</p> <p>Add some water as needed to make the mixture loosen up and turn a bit glossy. It can just hang out until you’re ready to eat.</p> <p>When you’re close to eating, pop your potatoes in the oven.</p> <p>Once they’re roasty toasty, add a knob of butter and some ranch seasoning. Toss to combine. (If you don’t have ranch seasoning, just use melted butter, fresh garlic, and dill. UNREAL.)</p> <p>Load it onto a soft bun – we love this with ranch potatoes and green beans!</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>Easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. We love these with Ranch Potatoes!</p> <p>White garlic sauce (for dipping, as shown in the video): Whisk 1/4 cup mayo, 1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, 1 clove grated garlic, 1-2 tablespoons water, and salt to taste.</p> <p>Making Ahead: The meat mixture is ready to go right after you add the ketchup and BBQ sauce, but I usually like to let it simmer for 30-60 minutes to really caramelize around the edges and deepen in both flavor and color. It also works perfectly to keep it warm in the crockpot after cooking!</p> <p>Keywords: sloppy joe’s, sloppy joe sandwiches, easy dinner, kid-friendly dinner</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>This was absolutely delicious. I need to add this to my regular rotation. Huge hit with the family!</p> <p>Sloppy Joe’s with ranch potatoes is a weeknight plate that still has a few moving parts — the sauced filling, the bun, and a side that has to land at the same time. Krillion, a themed movie trivia dive, uses that kind of stacking: several conditions at once, and a less common accepted title scores farther than the first hit everyone already knows.</p> <p>This was a hit with my family. The ranch potatoes are such a smart side with the sloppy joes. I will make this again soon.</p> <p>The sloppy Joes were delicious and easy! I love the idea of adding beef bullion. It definitely made it taste richer. I bought a jar of that for this recipe, along with the gorgeous brioche buns, at Costco. Be prepared to add a little more water at the end. I needed to add more to make it glossy and less sticky. This will be in our regular rotation!</p> <p>Yay – glad you loved in April! I agree about the water, I’m going to update that amount. I often need a bit more as well!</p> <p>My children all ate two helpings. This never happens. And those ranch potatoes are life changing.</p> <p>Amazing! It’s the best feeling! Thanks Lauren! 🙂 🙂</p> <p>This is a simple but delicious and nostalgic recipe. I made this last night and it was a hit.</p> <p>Do you have a favorite BBQ sauce for this recipe? I’m a vegetarian so can’t taste the recipe for my family – would love a recommendation!</p> <p>I’ve used the Trader Joe’s BBQ sauce for the last few batches and I really like it! 🙂</p> <p>Hi Linda! I have used a few kinds! Most frequent ones I’ve used are Trader Joe’s Kansas City BBQ sauce, or Famous Dave’s! 🙂</p> <p>This is such a throwback to the delicious sloppy joes of my childhood, I can already taste them! I’m a vegetarian now- any suggestion of what could be used in place of the meat? Wondering if a combo of beans and mushrooms might work…. off to do some research…. 🙂</p> <p>Hi Gigi: we are also mostly vegetarian (no red meat) so I make tofu crumbles. You can find a recipe on the internet. I freeze my tofu, thaw and drain it and then shred it on the large holes of a grater. Mix with seasonings and bake in the oven. I make a big batch and then seperate them into portions and freeze. Use them for this and anything else calling for ground beef. Hope this helps.</p> <p>Thanks for this! how would you adjust this if you wanted to create this and prep ahead of time, and serve later the next day in a crockpot?</p> <p>Jumping in to add that I also frequently 1.5x or 2x this and freeze whatever we don’t eat, since it works so well as a make-ahead! Especially when I know I’m going to be hosting or serving a crowd. Then I just reheat with a bit more water and sauce or warm in the crockpot.</p> <p>Make as is, then just put on low in a crockpot to rewarm!</p> <p>Ahhhhh Sloppy Joe’s!! My kids are now in their mid-20’s and these are STILL a family favorite haha. I love making them a nostalgic meal when they’re home. Can’t wait to try your version with the beef bouillon base…sounds like a perfect addition!</p> <p>It’s so funny, I make all of this (what I think is) interesting, fun, delicious food, but then I make just regular ol Sloppy Joe’s and my family is just swooning. 🙂 Hope my kids still want me to make these for them when they’re 20!</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Favorite things include my camera, lake days, and dark chocolate.</p> <p>Get a Free eCookbook with our top 25 recipes.</p> <p>The eBook includes our most popular 25 recipes in a beautiful, easy to download format. Deathbed portrait of Vanessa Bell by Duncan Grant discovered</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://cdn.sanity.io/images/cxgd3urn/production/ffb0624cc63a90a7528c36db884aa84573d71bd5-5000x6536.jpg?rect=0,1408,5000,3000&w=1200&h=720&q=85&fit=crop&auto=format" alt="Deathbed portrait of Vanessa Bell by Duncan Grant discovered" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Duncan Grant, Portrait of Vanessa Bell (1961)</p> <p>A poignant portrait of the artist Vanessa Bell, made within days of her death in 1961 by her sometime lover and lifelong friend Duncan Grant, has been rediscovered among family papers and donated to the famous home of the Bloomsbury Group, Charleston farmhouse in East Sussex.</p> <p>The drawing in soft pencil and biro, from an angle suggesting Grant was sitting by her bedside, was rediscovered among family papers during research for a forthcoming exhibition of the work of both artists at Tate Britain. It may have been made just after Bell’s death, though she could just be resting peacefully with eyes closed.</p> <p>Although Grant has dated the drawing “Friday April 14”, Bell actually died at the farmhouse on a week prior. In a statement from Charleston, now a museum and archive, Darren Clarke, head of collections and research, says that in later years, Grant and his friends went through masses of the work in his studio identifying and labelling pictures, so the date may have been added in error years later.</p> <p>“What seems very likely here is that Duncan knew this drawing had been made around Vanessa’s death and later added a date from memory. He got remarkably close, but apparently not quite close enough. Everything about the drawing itself – its viewpoint, its intimacy and its extraordinary economy – suggests someone sitting quietly beside Vanessa’s bed and drawing the face he had known for half a century.”</p> <p>The friendship and artistic partnership of Grant and Bell was one of the happiest and longest lasting of the tangled affairs of the group. Although Grant was gay and a former lover of Bell’s brother Adrian, they were lovers for a time and in 1918 had a child, Angelica—who went on to marry David Garnett, another of Grant’s lovers. Grant and Bell lived and worked at the 17th-century farmhouse for decades, covering many of the interiors with striking painted decoration. He outlived her by 17 years, and in 1978 was buried beside her in the churchyard of St Peter’s in Firle, near their home.</p> <p>Grant was long regarded as the most talented artist of the group, and the first major solo exhibition of Bell’s work came only in 2017 at the Dulwich Picture Gallery. At that time most of her paintings in the Tate collection were languishing in storage, but her reputation has been growing steadily in recent years. The Tate is making amends with a major exhibition of work by both artists, Vanessa Bell and Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury (12 November 2026 - 11 April 2027) at Tate Britain.</p> <p>Although Charleston is the largest lender to the Tate exhibition, including the entire contents of Grant’s studio, the drawing will only be included in the exhibition catalogue. It will go on public display for the first time at Charleston in May 2027, when the studio reopens after major conservation work.</p> <p>The drawing has been donated to Charleston as part of the 50 for 50 campaign which aims to bring 50 major works by the group back to the farmhouse in time for 2030, the 50th anniversary of the founding of the Charleston Trust, which runs and maintains the museum.</p> <p>Nathaniel Hepburn, the director and CEO of Charleston, says in a statement on the discovery: “I found this drawing deeply moving when I first saw it. We know Duncan’s drawings of Vanessa so intimately, made over the course of their long friendship, that the discovery of a previously unknown work is remarkable in itself. But there is something incredibly poignant about imagining Duncan sitting beside Vanessa, drawing her after her death.“</p> <p>The London exhibition, which opens 12 November, will explore the artistic and personal relationship between two of the Bloomsbury Group's most famous painters</p> <p>British artist Hew Locke has been selected for Tate Britain’s Duveen Galleries commission, while Barbara Hepworth gets a survey at Tate St Ives</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/11/04/deathbed-portrait-of-vanessa-bell-by-duncan-grant-discovered" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9585"> <h2>#9585. This Week In Psychology: Patience, Memory And Mental Health (P)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/glass-brain.jpg" alt="This Week In Psychology: Patience, Memory And Mental Health (P)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The week’s psychology highlights, from patience and success to changing memories, plus emerging studies beyond PsyBlog’s headlines.</p> <p>This week’s roundup brings together highlights from articles published on PsyBlog, alongside other studies in the news worth your attention.</p> <p>Several findings challenge familiar assumptions: patience gives entrepreneurs an advantage, ageing memories gain meaning as they lose detail, and physical activity does not always carry the same benefits for the brain.</p> <p>• Read members-only and premium content • Access courses • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/cannabis4-1.jpg" alt="8 Cannabis Risks That Can Follow Young People Into Adulthood (P)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Cannabis can affect the brain and mental health in surprising ways, with some risks appearing particularly concerning for teenagers.</p> <p>Cannabis is often seen as relatively harmless, especially compared with other drugs.</p> <p>But its effects may be particularly important during the teenage years, when the brain is still developing.</p> <p>Recent research suggests that using cannabis at this age may have consequences that last well beyond adolescence.</p> <p>Other studies suggest that negative effects on the brain and mental health may extend across the lifespan.</p> <p>• Read members-only and premium content • Access courses • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. Easy Eggplant Bolognese (1 Pot!)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://minimalistbaker.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Easy-Vegetarian-Eggplant-Bolognese-9.jpg" alt="Easy Eggplant Bolognese (1 Pot!)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Disclosure: This post may contain affiliate links which provide us a small commission when used for purchase. We're grateful for your support!</p> <p>When we add another bolognese to the blog (Yes, we already have versions 1, 2, 3, and 4), you know it’s something special! This newest version is made with EGGPLANT, meaning it’s the perfect bolognese for late summer. It’s light yet satisfying, creamy yet bright, and full of bold Italian-inspired flavor — everyone will be asking for seconds!</p> <p>Even better? It’s a breeze to make — just 1 pot required! What are you waiting for? Get that pasta water boiling!</p> <p>Bolognese is an Italian sauce that gets its name from the Italian city of Bologna. It’s typically made with meat, soffrito (onions, celery, and carrots), white wine, milk, and tomato paste or sauce, all simmered to create a rich, flavorful sauce.</p> <p>Our eggplant version strays from the traditional as it excludes meat (and includes eggplant) and incorporates dairy alternatives. But the rest of the dish is very similar to traditional bolognese and feels so hearty it might convert even the most adamant veggie skeptics!</p> <p>This 1-pot eggplant bolognese is everything you want for a cozy pasta night, minus the fuss! It starts with sautéing onion and carrots to create a simple, savory-sweet base. Next, we add eggplant (cut into very small cubes) and let it sauté until it has softened and browned (hello, flavor!).</p> <p>Build the flavor even further with garlic and red pepper flakes and by deglazing the pan with wine. Crushed tomatoes and tomato paste ensure a bright, tomato-forward sauce, and a small amount of dairy-free milk (we like homemade cashew milk) gives it a gentle creaminess and richness. The final flavor touches include dried Italian herbs (basil + oregano), sea salt, and maple syrup to balance the acidity of the tomatoes.</p> <p>Once all the ingredients are in your pan, it’s time to let the heat do its magic. Simmering for at least 20-30 minutes allows the sauce to thicken and concentrates the flavors as liquid evaporates away. If you have the time, you can let it continue simmering for up to an hour for even more flavor!</p> <p>When it’s done simmering, you’ll be left with an oh-so delicious, plant-powered sauce perfect for serving with your favorite pasta! It would also be lovely over polenta and is elevated by garnishing with fresh basil and our homemade vegan parmesan cheese.</p> <p>We think you’ll LOVE this eggplant bolognese! It’s:RichSavoryCreamy yet brightLight yet satisfyingEasy to make& SO delicious!</p> <p>It’s the perfect dish for a late summer pasta night! While quick enough for a weeknight, it’s also impressive enough to serve to dinner guests, especially paired with our Simple Vegan Meatballs, Pesto Turkey Meatballs, or Chickpea Caesar Salad (30 Minutes!).</p> <p>If you try this recipe, let us know! Leave a comment, rate it, and don’t forget to tag a photo @minimalistbaker on Instagram. Thanks so much for sharing!</p> <p>I love the idea of turning eggplant into a hearty bolognese, especially when it can all be made in one pot. Eggplant can soak up so much flavor, so it seems like a really good fit for a rich tomato-based sauce. I also appreciate recipes like this that make a meat-free meal feel filling rather than like a compromise. Definitely adding this one to my list to try.</p> <p>THIS WAS SO EASY AND SO RICH! Speaking Faster Can Make You More Persuasive — Until This Happens</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/talk-negotation-1.jpg" alt="Speaking Faster Can Make You More Persuasive — Until This Happens" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Your best argument may lose its edge if listeners struggle to keep up with how quickly you deliver it.</p> <p>Your best argument may lose its edge if listeners struggle to keep up with how quickly you deliver it.</p> <p>Speaking at a lively pace can make a strong argument more convincing, but rushing can weaken its impact.</p> <p>Very fast speech makes it harder for listeners to weigh up what they hear, reducing the advantage that good reasons have over weak ones.</p> <p>The findings suggest that persuading someone depends partly on giving them enough opportunity to think.</p> <p>The conclusions come from six experiments involving almost 4,000 people who listened to persuasive messages delivered at different speeds.</p> <p>Across the experiments, increasing the pace from very slow speech initially improved impressions of the speaker’s confidence and encouraged closer consideration of the message.</p> <p>However, these benefits eventually weakened or reversed as the delivery became faster.</p> <p>This helps explain why simply telling someone to speak more quickly is incomplete advice.</p> <p>A faster delivery can make an argument easier to engage with until the listener begins struggling to keep up.</p> <p>Crucially, the consequences depend on whether the reasons being offered stand up to scrutiny.</p> <p>In the two main experiments, listeners heard a proposal that would allow university students to pay lower tuition fees in exchange for working part-time.</p> <p>Some heard strong arguments emphasising benefits such as smaller classes and better services.</p> <p>Others heard weak arguments that included reduced leisure time and superficial improvements to the campus.</p> <p>The recordings were digitally altered to change speaking speed while keeping other vocal features, such as pitch and intonation, unchanged.</p> <p>Participants then rated their support for the proposal, with some also recording the thoughts that had occurred to them while listening.</p> <p>The combined results showed that strong arguments gained an increasing advantage over weak ones as speech became faster, but lost some of that advantage at higher speeds.</p> <p>In other words, delivery affected how effectively listeners distinguished a convincing case from an unconvincing one.</p> <p>A central part of persuasion is how carefully people consider the reasons they are given.</p> <p>When listeners examine a message closely, they have more opportunity to recognise its strengths, spot its weaknesses and form their own reactions.</p> <p>This benefits a strong argument, while exposing the shortcomings of a weak one.</p> <p>Very fast delivery can interfere with that process, making the merits of the message less influential.</p> <p>The analyses suggested that changes in how easily listeners felt they could follow the reasoning helped explain this pattern.</p> <p>Although speaking speed also affected how confident the speaker sounded, confidence alone did not adequately explain the overall pattern.</p> <p>One possible reason very slow speech is less effective is that it makes sustaining attention more demanding, while excessively fast speech leaves too little time to absorb the content.</p> <p>The experiments tested seven speaking speeds, ranging from 113 to 218 words per minute, but did not establish one ideal pace.</p> <p>The most effective delivery is likely to depend on factors including the complexity of the message, the audience and the presence of distractions.</p> <p>The findings also concern recorded persuasive messages, so they do not establish a universal rule for every conversation or public speech.</p> <p>For someone presenting a strong case, the findings suggest keeping the delivery lively while giving listeners time to follow the reasoning.</p> <p>Rushing may reduce the very scrutiny that would otherwise make a good argument convincing.</p> <p>The study was published in the Journal of Nonverbal Behavior (Guyer et al., 2025).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. A little-known protein may be fueling Alzheimer’s — and scientists found a way to block it</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.sciencedaily.com/images/1920/neuroscience-brain-puzzle-alzheimers-dementia.webp" alt="A little-known protein may be fueling Alzheimer’s — and scientists found a way to block it" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Ursula Quitterer calls it "Compound 10," a chemical substance developed by her research team that could potentially slow the progression of Alzheimer's disease.</p> <p>Quitterer, Professor of Molecular Pharmacology at ETH Zurich, has so far tested the experimental treatment in mice. The results were encouraging. The nerve cell death typically associated with dementia slowed significantly, and the treated animals lived longer.</p> <p>The work behind the compound began nearly 20 years ago, when Quitterer received brain tissue samples from patients treated by a doctor and colleague at Ain Shams University Hospital in Cairo. The tissue had been removed during tumor surgery from people with dementia as well as non-dementia patients.</p> <p>Quitterer used those samples to investigate an enzyme called GRK2, which has long been a major focus of her research.</p> <p>GRK2 plays an important regulatory role in many human cells. It helps cells respond appropriately to signals, stress, and strain. The enzyme is active in organs including the heart and the brain, where it helps support normal nerve cell function.</p> <p>By analyzing the Cairo tissue samples at the molecular level and conducting experiments in mice, Quitterer and her colleagues uncovered evidence that GRK2 plays an important role in dementia. Their findings were recently published in the journal Cell Reports Medicine.</p> <p>GRK2 exists in cells in two forms. One is normal and functional, while the other has been inactivated by cellular metabolism.</p> <p>Quitterer's team found unusually large amounts of the inactive form in brain tissue from people with dementia. The researchers observed the same pattern in mice, specifically in a mouse model for Alzheimer's disease.</p> <p>They also discovered that inactive GRK2 can clump together inside brain cells during dementia. These aggregates collect on mitochondria (the "powerhouses" of the cells), where they can interfere with normal function and cause damage.</p> <p>"The GRK2 aggregates block the pores of the mitochondria, reducing the amount of energy they can supply and leading to a situation of stress inside the cells," Quitterer explains.</p> <p>The mouse experiments revealed another important effect. Inactive GRK2 appeared to increase production of amyloid beta, a protein fragment that is considered a main cause of Alzheimer's.</p> <p>That process can then feed back on itself. Amyloid beta places additional stress on nerve cells, and that stress encourages the formation of more inactive GRK2 and more GRK2 aggregates. The result is a vicious circle that can contribute to the progression of dementia.</p> <p>To interrupt this process, Quitterer and her colleagues created several chemical compounds and tested them in cell cultures and mice.</p> <p>Compound 10 stood out as particularly effective. It prevented GRK2 molecules from forming aggregates, which allowed mitochondria to function better. The researchers also saw less amyloid beta accumulating in cells, while nerve cells were better able to maintain their function and avoid dying.</p> <p>The effects were not limited to the brain.</p> <p>In mice, compound 10 also had a positive effect on heart function and aging processes. One visible example was that older animals developed fewer grey hairs.</p> <p>The broader effects of compound 10 suggest that interfering with GRK2 aggregation may influence more than Alzheimer's related processes.</p> <p>In addition to protecting nerve cells and supporting mitochondrial function, the compound appeared to benefit the heart and affect some signs of aging in the mice.</p> <p>These findings remain preclinical, however. Compound 10 has not yet been developed into a treatment for people.</p> <p>The researchers have applied for a patent covering compound 10, and the basic research phase has now been completed.</p> <p>"It took so long simply because everything takes so long in Alzheimer's research," explains Quitterer.</p> <p>Because Alzheimer's is an age-related disease, the team needed to conduct experiments using older animals. In mice, that means working with animals that are about one and a half to two years old.</p> <p>Each experiment can also require roughly one and a half to two years before researchers have enough information to draw conclusions and design the next study.</p> <p>"It's all a great deal slower than in cancer research, for example."</p> <p>Quitterer and ETH Zurich are now searching for a company interested in helping move the compound toward the next stages of drug development.</p> <p>A Different Approach to Treating Alzheimer's</p> <p>"Alzheimer's is a very complex disease," says Quitterer.</p> <p>Existing medications do not cure Alzheimer's. At best, they can delay its progression by several months.</p> <p>"That's why it's so important that we've now identified a new target protein in the form of GRK2, as well as an active ingredient that operates via GRK2 and therefore via a different mechanism than existing Alzheimer's drugs."</p> <p>Because compound 10 acts through a different biological pathway, the researchers believe it could potentially complement existing treatments rather than replace them.</p> <p>Using compound 10 alongside other medications may one day help improve quality of life for people with Alzheimer's disease.</p> <p>Materials provided by ETH Zurich.
